messages:
incident-bot: :warning: High error rate detected: model_warmup_failures for 'redwood-llama-70b-q5' in eu-west-1. Count=62 in 10m. Top symptoms: 'compile timeout', 'deserialization checksum error', 'driver panic: GPU reset', container restart loops. Incident INC-2026-238 auto-created.

maya (SRE): ack. I'm seeing node flaps on node-zw-12 and several pods in CrashLoopBackOff. Kernel dmesg shows repeated I/O errors to ephemeral disk followed by kworker stalls. Collecting logs and system traces now.

alex (on-call): Copy. Attaching recent runtime logs from pod model-worker-70b-9c7a:

alex (on-call): ```
[2026-03-16T02:12:01Z] runtime: starting warmup for model redwood-llama-70b-q5
[2026-03-16T02:12:02Z] artifact: opening /models/llama-70b-v2/artifact.tar
[2026-03-16T02:12:10Z] artifact: checksum verify failed (manifest=0x7f4e..., computed=0x7f4f...)
[2026-03-16T02:12:11Z] deserial: EOF while mapping shard 3
[2026-03-16T02:12:12Z] compile: kernel select timeout after 30s (seq_len=4096)
[2026-03-16T02:12:13Z] nvml: GPU 0 panic: GPU reset detected
[2026-03-16T02:12:13Z] runtime: container terminated, exitCode=137 (OOM?)
[2026-03-16T02:12:15Z] kubelet: Evicting pod due to OOM_kill
```

maya (SRE): Interesting mix: artifact checksum mismatch + compile timeouts + GPU reset. Could be bad artifact plus a kernel path that tries heavy JIT/compiles causing driver to hit a bug and reset. Also the ephemeral disk I/O errors are suspicious (could corrupt artifact reads mid-stream).

luis (eng-runtime): On the runtime side: we recently pushed a change to aggressive JIT compilation for long sequences (PR #4821) which increases temporary GPU scratch allocations. If a partial artifact read occurs, deserial will hit EOF and the subsequent compile might be given bad pointers -> driver panic. Short-term: we should disable JIT/compile for that model and force CPU-side deserialization. Also mark artifact as quarantine until we re-verify in object store.

taylor (eng-platform): I can push a quick control-plane toggle to disable model-level compile and increase fallback to the smaller 'llama-70b-q4' variant. Also I'll check the node pool storage health: talking to infra to check ephemeral disk SMART metrics and mount options.

maya (SRE): Mitigation plan executing now:
- disable runtime JIT for redwood-llama-70b-q5
- set route to route-abc to send 90% traffic to llama-70b-q4 and 10% to q5 for sanity checks
- cordon node-zw-12 and drain pods to healthy nodes
- raise minReplicas and pause autoscaler

maya (SRE): commands I'm running:
```bash
# disable JIT/compile for model
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://console.api.redwood.ai/v1/models/redwood-llama-70b-q5/config -d '{"runtime": {"enable_jit": false, "deserial_on_cpu": true}}'
# update route weights
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://console.api.redwood.ai/v1/routes/route-abc/patch -d '{"route":[{"model":"redwood-llama-70b-q4","weight":90},{"model":"redwood-llama-70b-q5","weight":10}]}'
```

deploy-bot: rollout: controller: deployment/model-worker-70b successful (3 -> 4 replicas).

support-ops: Customer impact: three customers reported elevated 500s for completions endpoints over the past 20m (ACCT-9001, ACCT-9002, ACCT-9003). No data exfiltration reported. Support message drafted and queued.

alex (on-call): After mitigations, new pods are coming up on healthy nodes but still seeing transient kube OOM events on overloaded nodes. I cordoned node-zw-12 and drained it; infra confirms a disk controller error was observed at ~02:08 UTC.

luis (eng-runtime): Forensics steps: 1) re-compute checksums of S3 objects and compare to manifests; 2) run artifact rehydrate job that streams to /tmp with strict verification before mounting into container; 3) collect GPU kernel logs (nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY, nvml stacks) from affected nodes. If artifact corrupted in S3, restore from backup snapshot.

maya (SRE): I've attached initial artifacts to INC-2026-238 (S3 manifests, pod logs, dmesg). Also captured a core dump from one of the crashed containers and uploaded to secure bucket.

taylor (eng-platform): infra ticket created: INFRA-3245: investigate faulty ephemeral disk and disk controller alerts in eu-west-1 zone b. Replacing node-zw-12 and running disk health diag. Also enabling server-side checks on artifact upload path to reject partial uploads (md5+size).

luis (eng-runtime): Long term runtime fixes listed in INC: add pre-read artifact validation that rejects warmup if checksum mismatch; fall back to CPU deserial and avoid any GPU JIT compile until artifact validated; add circuit breaker to stop warmup if sequential failures exceed threshold.

maya (SRE): Handing off to alex for night watch. Summary for handoff -> INC-2026-238: root symptoms: disk/controller I/O errors caused partial artifact reads -> checksum mismatch & deserial EOF -> runtime tried aggressive JIT compile -> GPU driver panic and OOM kills -> node/pod flapping. Mitigations applied: JIT disabled for q5, CPU deserial enabled, traffic shifted to q4, node cordoned and drained, minReplicas increased, autoscaler paused, artifact quarantined. Customer impact: 3 paying customers saw transient 5xxs; support notified and status page updated.

alex (on-call): ACK, taking over. Next actions: monitor error rate for next 2 hours, gather S3 checksums and compare, coordinate with infra to confirm node replacement, and follow-up with eng-runtime tomorrow for the runtime hardening plan. If errors spike again, @pager oncall.

support-ops: Posted status update to status.redwood.ai: "Partial failures for llama-70b-q5 in eu-west-1; mitigations in place; short-term traffic rerouted; investigation ongoing. Affected customers have been contacted."

incident-bot: INC-2026-238 created and assigned to on-call: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2026-238

alex (on-call): Closing triage here unless new failures surface. Will keep thread open and update incident ticket with forensic artifacts. :white_check_mark:
